# the contributor audit: sharp positive-circuit triangle-cap incidence threshold



The theorem concerns an actual ordinary triangle, an interior source, and three rank-two positively dependent through-source normals. It does not claim that an arbitrary middle body is triangular, or that its menu is genuinely mixed-critical.

For a cap strictly capturing two vertices, the omitted-corner intercept relation and captured area formula are correct. Differentiation gives strict concavity in the intercept parameter. Moving toward the endpoint in the derivative-selected direction keeps area nonincreasing. The positive-circuit direction cone and the fixed-incidence direction cone each have angular width less than pi, so their relevant intersection is an interval. If a limiting direction exited the circuit cone, its normal would be opposite to a fixed normal. The two ordinary closed cap fractions would then sum to one because the boundary line has zero area, contradicting both fractions being below one half. Thus an actual vertex incidence is reached, with the circuit retained. At most three such rotations suffice, because fixed caps do not change their own incidences.

The positive dependence and rank force each triangle vertex to be strictly captured by at least one cap. Once each cap strictly captures only one vertex, these assignments are consequently distinct. The barycentric intercept inequality q>=4 alpha beta and its refinement q>=beta/(1-alpha) when alpha>=1/2 are correct. Applying the refinement to the other two caps proves all three source barycentric coordinates are below one half.

For the remaining cap through a vertex, its exact fraction is z/(x+z). The scalar ranges in t=z/x and x are correct. The concavity endpoint bound rules out t<=1/2. For t>1/2, the increasing and concave lower bounds meet at x=1/(1+2t), yielding 4t/(1+2t)^2. This function decreases on the relevant interval, and substitution of t<=c/(1-c) gives c^2+6c-3>=0 exactly. Thus every cap must have one distinct captured vertex and no other boundary vertex below c0=2sqrt(3)-3.

The sharpness margins vanish at the stated source; their displayed positive linear combination is identically zero in all three barycentric coefficients. Their normals have rank two. The second and third cap intercepts are exactly (2x,2z) and (2x,2y), and all three cap fractions equal c0. The rational comparison 128/279<c0 has the stated exact positive squared gap 2867.

No limiting body, mass-bearing mixed boundary, lattice map, or unproved minimizing-shape principle is used in this ordinary theorem. It supplies only its stated incidence conclusion.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
